title: Esther
summary: Esther is a biblical book focused on diaspora vulnerability, courage, reversal, and providence.
historical_context: Esther tells how Jewish life in the Persian diaspora is preserved through courage, reversal, and hidden providence.
ancient_near_east_context: Esther belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Esther should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Esther as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Historical Books, book 12 of 12, Esther contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting diaspora vulnerability, courage, reversal, and providence to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Esther as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Esther uses narrative within Historical Books, book 12 of 12 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Esther helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Many scholars read the books as later historiographical or Deuteronomistic shaping
date_ranges: Historical span from settlement through exile
Final form often placed in the exilic or post-exilic period
original_audience: Israel and Judah remembering the land, monarchy, and exile
historical_setting: Settlement, monarchy, and exile in the land of Israel and Judah
canonical_role: Esther anchors diaspora vulnerability, courage, reversal, and providence within Historical Books, book 12 of 12 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How conquest, kingship, and exile are narrated theologically

related_objects.notes: Esther is the central figure in the court deliverance narrative.
Mordecai shapes the crisis and reversal.
Persia is the imperial setting for the book.
Susa is the court setting for the narrative.
The book is commonly read through God's hidden providence.
